bib.title: Language Models Are Greedy Reasoners: A Systematic Formal Analysis of Chain-of-Thought

read.skipped: reference list skimmed; figure bar heights are not in the text layer

question: Can LLMs actually reason with chain-of-thought, judged by formally checking each predicted proof step rather than the final label?
hypothesis: Label accuracy on real-world tasks may hide heuristics or retrieval, so step-level proof analysis on a synthetic fictional-ontology task will show where reasoning fails.
contributions: PRONTOQA, a synthetic first-order-logic QA dataset with unique parseable proofs and programmable difficulty
A formal step-level analysis of InstructGPT/GPT-3 chains of thought (valid/atomic/misleading step taxonomy)
Finding that models make valid individual steps but fail at proof planning when several valid steps exist

method.summary: Examples are generated from random linear ontologies and modus-ponens proofs, rendered in simple natural language. OpenAI GPT-3 family models are prompted 8-shot with CoT under greedy decoding; each predicted CoT sentence is semantically parsed and classified as valid/atomic/misleading against the gold proof.
method.task: synthetic deductive true/false QA with chain-of-thought proof evaluation

datasets.name: PRONTOQA
datasets.split: no train/test split; examples generated on the fly; 8 in-context examples per prompt, all i.i.d. from the generator
datasets.preprocessing: distractor sentence added at a random position in the context (a new disconnected concept with the negation of the queried property) to block lookup shortcuts; ontologies are linear, 3 to 10 concepts; query is the conclusion or its negation with probability 0.5

models.name: text-davinci-002 (InstructGPT)
models.context: inferred: roughly twice the 2049-token limit of 001 models

models.name: text-ada-001, text-babbage-001, text-curie-001, davinci, text-davinci-001
models.params: 350M, 1.3B, 6.7B mentioned for the first three (text of section 5.3)

inference.samples: 400 examples per configuration; 1 greedy output each; self-consistency 40 samples per example on 100 examples
inference.prompting: 8-shot in-context CoT: 8 fully-labeled questions then one test question; CoT sentences are atomic gold proof steps

parameters.ontology type: fictional, true (3 hand-coded real ontologies), false (random real names)
parameters.DFS experiment: in-context CoTs follow depth-first search incl. misleading steps; 100 examples, 5 hops fictional top-down

other.api_dates: main runs 9-11 Sep 2022; self-consistency 29-30 Oct 2022; DFS 16 Nov 2022

metrics.name: strict proof accuracy
metrics.definition: a path of canonical (strictly-valid atomic correct) steps reaches the conclusion

metrics.name: skip proof accuracy
metrics.definition: path may include strictly-valid non-atomic correct steps

metrics.name: valid proof accuracy
metrics.definition: path may include strictly- or broadly-valid steps

baselines: model size ladder from text-ada-001 to text-davinci-002
eval.protocol: 95% Wilson confidence intervals; number of correct proofs ~ Binomial(400, p); unparseable steps count as incorrect

availability.data: generator and all model outputs at github.com/asaparov/prontoqa

prompts.text:
Q: Each cat is a carnivore. Every carnivore is not herbivorous. Carnivores are mammals. All mammals are warm-blooded. Mammals are vertebrates. Every vertebrate is an animal. Animals are multicellular. Fae is a cat. True or false: Fae is not herbivorous.
A: Fae is a cat. Cats are carnivores. Fae is a carnivore. Every carnivore is not herbivorous. Fae is not herbivorous. True
prompts.where: Fig 1, p2 (the actual experiments use fictional names such as wumpus)

results.claim: Most predicted proof steps from text-davinci-002 are strictly valid (5-hop fictional ontology).
results.setup: text-davinci-002, 8-shot CoT, greedy, 5 hops, fictional ontology
results.quote: 93.2% of proof steps are strictly-valid, 2.4% are broadly-valid, and 5.9% are invalid
results.note: the three shares sum to 101.5% as printed; 2.4% of steps are also stated to be non-atomic

results.claim: Invalid steps are a small share of steps.
results.quote: 93.2% of proof steps are strictly-valid, 2.4% are broadly-valid, and 5.9% are invalid

results.claim: Self-consistency (40 samples, T=0.7) does not improve valid proof accuracy.
results.quote: The resulting valid proof accuracy is 0.56 compared to 0.545 which is not

results.claim: In-context depth-first-search traces do not improve valid proof accuracy.
results.quote: The resulting valid proof accuracy is 0.55 compared to 0.545 which

results.claim: Only text-davinci-002 beats chance; accuracy rises from 350M to 1.3B and 6.7B.
results.note: bar heights only in figure; no numbers in text

results.claim: With a true ontology accuracy is much higher and does not drop from 3 to 5 hops; fictional and false ontologies are comparable (false slightly worse).
5-hop top-down fictional accuracy falls to chance; 1 and 3 hops are handled well; top-down is harder than bottom-up as hops grow.
The first non-canonical step in incorrect proofs is most often a strictly-valid atomic misleading step; models walk valid edges but pick the wrong branch and rarely recover (planning failure).
Label accuracy correlates poorly with strict proof accuracy and best with valid proof accuracy across the 48 experiments.

limits: Only modus ponens, proofs of at most 5 hops, semantically simple sentences and linear ontologies; may not extend to longer proofs, other rules or complex sentences (conclusion).
Models are 2022 OpenAI API models (GPT-3 family, text-davinci-002) and are dated; no later models evaluated.
Authors could not determine why text-davinci-002 greatly outperforms 001 versions; suggest token limit as one factor.
Most headline results are bar charts only; text gives few numbers.
Self-consistency and DFS tested on only 100 examples in one configuration.
Authors say CoT is not sufficient for harder (mathematical) reasoning and suggest neurosymbolic search, but do not test it.

terms.definition: provable from previous steps with exactly one application of a gold-proof deduction rule and part of the gold proof path
a step whose premises are part of the gold proof but whose conclusion is not
provable only with a more powerful calculus than the gold proofs use (here, transitivity of subtype)
fraction of proofs (not steps) containing a path of allowed step types from premises to the conclusion

code.snippet: evaluate_cot / is_provable: parse each predicted sentence to a logical form, test provability from context and prior conclusions, mark misleading if premises are in the gold proof but conclusion is not; correct iff the final gold conclusion is provable
